source_text: Credimus etiam inde uenturum conuenientissimo tempore et iudicaturum uiuos et mortuos. siue istis nominibus iusti et peccatores significentur, siue quos tunc ante mortem in terris inuenturus est, appellati sint uiui, mortui uero, qui in eius aduentu resurrecturi sunt, haec dispensatio temporalis non tantum est sicut illa generatio secundum deum, sed etiam fuit et erit. nam fuit dominus noster in terris et nunc est in caelo et erit in claritate iudex uiuorum atque mortuorum. ita enim ueniet, sicut ascendit, secundum auctoritatem, quae apostolorum actibus continetur. ex hac itaque temporali dispensatione loquitur in Apocalypsi, ubi scriptum est: haec dicit qui est et qui fuit et qui uenturus est.
thought_title: The Son's coming as judge in the earthly mission
orientation: Augustine is still expounding the article on Christ's session at the right hand and now explains the creed's next clause about his coming to judge the living and the dead.
pass_a_gloss: We believe also [that] from there [he] will come at [the] most fitting time and [that he] will judge [the] living and [the] dead. whether by these names [the] just and [the] sinners are signified, or [those] whom then before death on [the] earth [he] is going to find, [they] may have been called living, [the] dead however, who at his coming [are] going to rise again, this temporal dispensation not only is as that generation according to God, but also was and will be. for was our Lord on [the] earth and now is in heaven and will be in glory judge of [the] living and of [the] dead. for so [he] will come, just as [he] ascended, according to [the] authority, which in [the] acts of [the] apostles is contained. from this therefore temporal dispensation [he] speaks in [the] Apocalypse, where [it] has been written: these things says [he] who is and who was and who is to come.

choices.why: The glossary requires this rendering for God's saving plan carried out in time through Christ's incarnation, death, and resurrection.
This refers back to the eternal generation of the Son treated earlier, so 'begetting' preserves the contrast with the earthly mission.

pass_b_english: We also believe that he will come from there at the most fitting time and will judge the living and the dead. Whether these names mean the just and the sinners, or whether those whom he will find on earth before death at his coming are called the living, and the dead are those who will rise again at his arrival, this earthly mission is not merely as that generation according to God is, but it also was and will be. For our Lord was on earth, and now he is in heaven, and he will be in glory as judge of the living and of the dead. For he will come just as he ascended, according to the authority contained in the Acts of the Apostles. From this earthly mission, then, he speaks in Revelation, where it is written: These things says he who is and who was and who is to come (Revelation 1:4).

last_rejected.ruling: 'Earthly mission' fits 'dispensatio temporalis'; English preserves 'not only...but also was and will be.' Clause intact, no major error.
